To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concomitant delivery or pretreatment with immunomodulator, tuftsin can combat less susceptible candidiasis in neutropenic mice.
co-administration of immunostimulant tuftsin and antimicrobial agents can effectively combat fungal infections in temporarily neutropenized mice.
the immunomodulatory activity of tuftsin can be exploited in combination with antifungal liposomes to combat candidiasis in mice with temporarily compromised immune functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunomodulators-based therapy against deep-seated fungal diseases.
the role of liposomisation in the delivery of immunomodulators and antimicrobial agents in the host.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches to combat fungal diseases in neutropenic subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
co-administration of liposomified tuftsin and polyene antibiotics can be considered as a potential therapeutic option for the treatment of candidiasis in patients with neutropenia.
the immunomodulatory tuftsin can effectively contribute to the elimination of less susceptible C. albicans in temporarily neutropogenic Balb/c mice.
co-administration of immunoadjuvant tuftsin and antifungals (liposomal nystatin and am-photericin B in this case) can combat less susceptible C. albicans infections in temporarily neutropogenic mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tuftsin can act as an adjunctive agent to the polyenes in combating candidiasis in the temporarily neutropenic hosts.
tuftsin is an important adjunct to antifungal chemotherapy in temporarily neutropenia.
the co-administration of liposomized tuftsin and polyene antibiotics (nysatin and amphotercin B) could be used as an effective strategy to treat candidiasis in neutropenic patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunomodulator-tuftsin can be used in the management of opportunistic infections in neutropenic hosts.
tuftsin can be used as a potential chemotherapeutic agent in conjunction with liposomal polyenes to treat candidiasis and possibly other fungal infections in temporarily neutropogenic patients.
the immunomodulators such as tuftsin can be used as a potential adjunct to the conventional antimicrobial therapy for the treatment of fungal infections in temporarily neutropenia.
